quick: Glaucoma 250 mg-1 g/day divided; altitude 125-250 mg BID
May take with food to reduce GI upset
Avoid in first trimester; use only if clearly needed
summary: Acetazolamide is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor used for open-angle and acute glaucoma, certain epilepsies, edema and prevention of acute mountain sickness. Oral dosing ranges from 250 mg to 1 g daily. It causes a metabolic acidosis and bicarbonate diuresis; monitor electrolytes and avoid in sulfonamide allergy.
indications: Chronic simple (open-angle) glaucoma and secondary glaucoma
Preoperative management of acute angle-closure glaucoma to lower intraocular pressure
Adjunctive treatment of edema due to congestive heart failure and drug-induced edema
Centrencephalic epilepsies (petit mal, unlocalized seizures) as adjunct
Prevention or amelioration of symptoms of acute mountain sickness

dosage.d: 250 mg to 1 g/day, divided for doses over 250 mg
250 mg every 4 h, or 250 mg BID; may give 500 mg then 125-250 mg q4h
250-375 mg once daily in the morning
8-30 mg/kg/day in divided doses; usual 375-1000 mg/day
dosage.n: Titrate; tolerance to effect may develop

dosage.d: 125-250 mg twice daily (500 mg ER once daily)
dosage.n: Start 24-48 h before ascent, continue 48 h at altitude

admin: Take orally; may be given with food to reduce GI irritation
Sustained-release capsules are for glaucoma and altitude prophylaxis, not for epilepsy or diuresis
Begin altitude prophylaxis 24-48 hours before ascent and continue while at altitude
Maintain adequate hydration and monitor serum potassium and bicarbonate
Intermittent or alternate-day dosing helps preserve diuretic response
moa: Acetazolamide reversibly inhibits the enzyme carbonic anhydrase, reducing formation of carbonic acid and decreasing availability of hydrogen and bicarbonate ions. In the eye this lowers aqueous humor formation and intraocular pressure; in the kidney it increases excretion of bicarbonate, sodium, potassium and water (alkaline diuresis); and CNS effects retard abnormal neuronal discharge. The induced metabolic acidosis aids acclimatization at altitude.

absolute: Marked hepatic disease or cirrhosis (risk of hepatic encephalopathy)
relative: Long-term use in chronic non-congestive angle-closure glaucoma

preg: Acetazolamide is teratogenic in animals at high doses. Avoid in the first trimester and use during pregnancy only when the potential benefit clearly justifies the risk.
lact: Acetazolamide is excreted in human milk in small amounts; use with caution while breastfeeding and monitor the infant.
renal: Contraindicated in marked renal impairment because reduced excretion can cause toxicity and the diuretic effect is diminished. Use cautiously and monitor electrolytes in lesser degrees of impairment.
hepatic: Contraindicated in marked hepatic disease and cirrhosis; the drug-induced alkalinization of urine can reduce ammonia excretion and precipitate hepatic encephalopathy.

major: High-dose aspirin/salicylates - severe metabolic acidosis and salicylate toxicity (can be fatal)
Other carbonic anhydrase inhibitors / topiramate - additive acidosis, metabolic and renal stone risk
moderate: Lithium - increased renal lithium excretion (reduced levels)
Amphetamines, quinidine, ephedrine - reduced renal clearance (urine alkalinization)
minor: Sodium bicarbonate - increased risk of renal calculi
interactions.food: May be taken with food; ensure adequate fluid intake.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; may worsen dehydration and CNS depression.
interactions.diagnostics: May produce false-positive urine protein tests; alters serum electrolytes and bicarbonate.

monitoring: Complete blood count periodically with long-term use
Signs of acidosis, rash or sulfonamide hypersensitivity
counsel: Tingling of hands/feet and a metallic taste are common and usually harmless
Drink plenty of fluids; report flank pain (possible kidney stones)
Report rash, sore throat, fever, easy bruising or yellowing of skin
May cause drowsiness; use caution driving
For altitude sickness, start 1-2 days before ascending
pearls: Sulfonamide derivative - avoid in sulfonamide allergy
Causes a self-limited metabolic acidosis that drives altitude acclimatization
Tolerance to the diuretic effect develops; intermittent dosing preserves response
Avoid with high-dose aspirin - risk of severe, potentially fatal acidosis
Alkalinizes urine - can predispose to calcium phosphate stones; maintain hydration
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the usual schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: No specific antidote. Overdose may cause electrolyte imbalance, metabolic acidosis, drowsiness and CNS effects. Treat supportively, correct acidosis and electrolytes; acetazolamide is dialyzable, so hemodialysis may be useful in severe cases or renal failure.
